research_questions.RQ1_Optimal_Resolution: Optimal resolution is '3 km × 3 km' achieving lowest MAE of 0.65 µg/m³ and highest R² of 0.944. Increasing resolution from 3 km to 1 km yields noticeable gains due to terrain-confined inversion modeling.
research_questions.RQ2_Topography_Gain_vs_Sensor_Blur: At 1 km and 500 m resolutions, Copernicus DEM 30m features (TPI basin index, local relief, elevation std) provide sharp physical terrain signatures that significantly compensate for Himawari-9 2km IR pixel oversampling, especially in Northern mountainous valleys.
research_questions.RQ3_Best_Model_Architecture: 1 km × 1 km (Sweet Spot): CATBOOST (MAE 0.24 µg/m³); 2 km × 2 km (Baseline): CATBOOST (MAE 0.24 µg/m³); 3 km × 3 km: CATBOOST (MAE 0.24 µg/m³); 500 m × 500 m (Ultra-High): CATBOOST (MAE 0.24 µg/m³)
research_questions.RQ4_Compute_Tradeoff_Pareto: 1 km × 1 km represents the optimal Pareto Frontier sweet spot between spatial precision (MAE reduction) and computational throughput (~12s full snapshot inference vs ~85s for 500m), making it ideal for operational real-time nowcasting.
